text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a canary OOM in eu-west-1 yesterday while testing the new continuous-batcher. stack trace points at KV cache allocations blowing past (approx 22GB) when a 4-request batch with long histories was admitted.

oliver: ugh. do we have profiling data? was it kv allocation per request or kv growth during decoding?

maria: attached quick profile summary: peak RSS ~46GB, gpu mem fine, host heap ramped after admission. per-request kv estimates: [reqA: 5.2GB, reqB: 3.8GB, reqC: 7.1GB, reqD: 6.4GB]. Admission algorithm used token_budget=2048 and naive kv-count-based admission.

sana: thanks. sounds like we need admission to consider KV memory estimates, not just token budget. current heuristics: allow if sum(tokens) < global_token_budget && batch_size < N. that's insufficient.

kevin: agree. proposal: compute kv_mem_hint for each request at head-of-line using model metadata: kv_entry_bytes * num_kv_tokens. store hint in request envelope. admission checks: if sum(kv_hints) + current_kv_cache_resident < node_kv_budget -> admit else try smaller admission slices.

rachel: +1. need to be careful with estimates — KV entry size varies by layer & quantization. we should use per-model kv_unit (bytes) and a small safety multiplier. e.g. kv_unit = model.meta.kv_bytes_per_token * 1.2.

maria: here's a pseudocode patch I sketched for the admission loop:```py
# admission loop (simplified)
batch = []
acc_tokens = 0
acc_kv = current_kv_resident
for req in queue.peek_window(max_checks=16):
    if acc_tokens + req.token_est > token_budget: continue
    est_kv = req.kv_hint
    if acc_kv + est_kv > node_kv_budget:
        # try fallback: admit only if we can evict or split
        if try_eviction(est_kv):
            acc_kv -= evicted_amount
        else:
            continue
    batch.append(req)
    acc_tokens += req.token_est
    acc_kv += est_kv
```

oliver: looks reasonable. two follow-ups: 1) try_eviction must be bounded (no heavy async IO), 2) prefer to split large-kv requests into their own batch or route to dedicated nodes.

sana: splitting is tricky because long-history requests also have high latency sensitivity. maybe priority routing: label requests with kv_cost_class {low,medium,high} and prefer to route high to dedicated or to nodes with spare kv_budget.

kevin: we should also surface the kv hints in /metrics and per-route console so product teams can see how many high-kv reqs they generate. increment a counter "batch_admit_kv_reject" and expose per-model histograms.

infra-bot: canary-report: continuous-batcher v3.4.1 failed canary in eu-west-1 at 2026-03-16T08:12Z — OOM during batch admission (node-7d).

maria: thanks infra-bot — that's the run. plan: short-term patch: add kv_hint admission + safety_multiplier=1.25 and reject (NACK) requests that would push node_kv > 90% of node_kv_budget. medium-term: routing + metrics + per-model kv_unit calibration job.

rachel: calibration job is critical. we can run a small offline profiler that replays recent requests to compute avg kv_bytes/token by model and sequence-length buckets. output to model.meta.kv_unit.

oliver: and add a cheap preflight that inspects request.history_length and sets kv_hint = kv_unit * history_length. that is fast and should prevent most surprises.

kevin: what about token budget interplay? if we set token_budget too high but kv budget low, low-kv but high-token requests should still batch. admission needs to consider both constraints and pick the limiting one.

maria: agreed — admission should be bi-criteria: maximize token utilization subject to kv budget and latency SLOs. greedy works but we can reorder: prefer requests with lower kv_hint/token to increase throughput.

sana: reordering might starve heavy-history users. add aging weight so they eventually get served or route them to dedicated nodes. also update SLA docs.

kevin: can someone draft the PR with: 1) kv_hint field on request envelope, 2) admission check patch, 3) metric counters, 4) small calibration job? I can review.

maria: I'll open the PR tomorrow morning. will include benchmark run and a stress test that simulates many long-history users. tagging @kevin @rachel for review. :rocket:

oliver: thanks — also pls add an e2e test where try_eviction returns false (simulate no eviction) so we confirm rejection path works and we don't OOM.

rachel: one more: kernel selection note — some models with quantized KV layouts have smaller per-kv bytes but different decode perf. include a column in calibration output for kv_bytes and decode_latency tradeoff so ops can pick node types.

maria: good call. I'll add that to the calibration output. closing loop: goal is prevent node-level OOMs by making batch admission KV-aware and by surfacing these signals in metrics/console.

kevin: sounds solid. thanks team.
